answer.summary: AI-generated content isn’t inherently bad for SEO: what matters is whether it is useful to users and supports their journey. Unhelpful filler can waste effort and contribute to low-quality content, while useful content—such as product descriptions or human-reviewed summaries—can be created with AI.

sections.heading: What matters instead
sections.content: Schwartz says AI is a tool, not a solution. The key test is the content’s helpfulness and usefulness to the user and their journey—not whether AI produced it. Recreating worthless content with AI does not make it valuable; using AI to make genuinely useful content more cheaply or effectively is reasonable.

These examples illustrate useful, reviewed or purpose-serving content—not a guarantee of SEO performance. He also notes that Google faces a growing volume of content and may clean its index to reduce costs and protect users from poor content.

answer.summary: AI itself isn’t the SEO problem; whether the content is genuinely useful to people and serves their journey matters more. AI can help produce useful content, while unnecessary or worthless material is still a problem regardless of how it was made.

sections.heading: What matters instead
sections.content: Schwartz says AI is a tool, not a solution. The key question is whether the content is helpful and useful to the user and part of their journey—not whether AI contributed to it. Using AI to make already-useful content more cheaply or better is reasonable; generating content merely for the sake of having more content can produce the same worthless material as cheap human-written content.

sections.heading: Examples and caveat
sections.content: For e-commerce, AI-written product descriptions that explain the product and useful features can help users and aren’t inherently harmful to SEO. By contrast, adding unnecessary “fluff” to category pages is a waste. Schwartz also describes AI drafting product reviews from information about 10 products for a human editor to review, and automated earnings-report summaries as examples of generated content that can still be useful. His point is about usefulness, not a guarantee that any AI-generated page will rank.
